test_cases.test_name: Verify Continuous Temperature Monitoring and Recording Intervals
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS continuously monitors temperature and records readings at the specified interval.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational in all GMP storage areas.
Access to EMS software and data logs.

test_steps.action: Observe the EMS software interface for a continuous period of at least 10 minutes.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings for all monitored areas are displayed and updated in real-time.
data_to_capture: Observed temperature values for each sensor

test_steps.action: Access the system's data logs or database and extract temperature readings for a specific monitored area over a 10-minute period.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are recorded at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes, as per URS-EMS-002.

acceptance_criteria: Temperature readings are continuously displayed and updated.
All recorded temperature readings are within the specified 5-minute interval.
No gaps in recorded data exceeding the 5-minute interval are observed.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be accurate and complete.
Timestamps must be precise and reliable.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Alarm Generation and Notification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS generates alerts when temperature deviates from the setpoint and that notifications are sent within the specified response time.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational.
Defined setpoints and alarm deviations are configured in the EMS.
Site paging system is operational and integrated.
Access to EMS software and alarm logs.

test_steps.action: Manually adjust a temperature sensor in a monitored area to simulate a deviation of +2°C from its setpoint.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm is generated within the EMS software, and an alert notification is sent to the designated personnel.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of alarm generation in EMS
Timestamp of notification received (e.g., email, SMS, page)

test_steps.action: Measure the time elapsed between the alarm generation in the EMS and the receipt of the notification.
test_steps.expected_result: The system response time for alarm conditions does not exceed 30 seconds.

test_steps.action: Return the temperature sensor to its normal operating range.
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm condition is cleared in the EMS software, and a clear notification is logged.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of temperature return to normal

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 1-3 for a temperature deviation of -2°C from the setpoint.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm is generated within the EMS software, and an alert notification is sent to the designated personnel within 30 seconds.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of alarm generation in EMS

acceptance_criteria: Alarms are generated when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint.
Alarm notifications are sent to the appropriate personnel.
System response time for alarm conditions is within 30 seconds.
Alarm clear notifications are logged.
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm events and notifications must be accurately logged with timestamps.
Notification delivery must be reliable.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Range Accuracy and Vendor Software Integrity
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system accurately monitors temperature within the specified range and that vendor-supplied software remains unmodified.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Access to system logs and configuration settings.
Calibrated temperature probes or reference thermometers.

test_steps.action: Introduce a calibrated temperature probe into a GMP storage area and set it to a known temperature within the specified range (-80°C to +50°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS system displays the temperature reading within ±0.5°C of the calibrated probe's reading.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS system's software installation directory and configuration files.
test_steps.expected_result: No unauthorized modifications or changes are detected in the vendor-supplied software files or configuration settings.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of software version and configuration files

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 1 and 2 for temperatures at the lower, middle, and upper bounds of the specified range.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are consistently within ±0.5°C of the calibrated probe at all tested points, and software remains unmodified.
data_to_capture: All data captured in steps 1 and 2 for each temperature point

acceptance_criteria: All temperature readings recorded by the EMS system are within ±0.5°C of the calibrated reference temperature.
No evidence of unauthorized modifications to the vendor-supplied software is found.
data_integrity_requirements: Accuracy of temperature readings is critical for product quality.
Ensuring vendor software integrity prevents unintended system behavior.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Storage and Retention Capabilities
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system can store data for the required duration and that the archival feature functions correctly.
prerequisites: EMS system is operational and collecting data.
Access to system administration and reporting tools.
Knowledge of the system's data storage capacity and archival process.

test_steps.action: Monitor system storage usage over a period of time, simulating continuous data collection.
test_steps.expected_result: The system's storage capacity is sufficient to support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring data.
data_to_capture: Projected storage full date based on current usage

test_steps.action: Initiate the vendor's archival feature for historical data.
test_steps.expected_result: The archival process completes successfully, and data is moved to the designated archival location.
data_to_capture: Confirmation message or log entry of successful archival

test_steps.action: Attempt to retrieve specific data points from the archived data.
test_steps.expected_result: The archived data is accessible and retrievable, maintaining its integrity and format.
data_to_capture: Specific data points requested from archive

test_steps.action: Verify that the system retains data for at least 7 years as per regulatory requirements.
test_steps.expected_result: The system's configuration and operational logs confirm that data retention policies are met.
data_to_capture: System configuration settings for data retention
Audit trail entries related to data retention

acceptance_criteria: System storage capacity is confirmed to support at least 10 years of continuous monitoring.
Archival process successfully moves data to the designated location.
Archived data is retrievable and maintains its integrity.
System configuration and logs confirm compliance with 7-year data retention.
data_integrity_requirements: Long-term data retention is essential for regulatory compliance and historical analysis.
Archival process must ensure data availability and integrity.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Electronic Signature Functionality and Audit Trail for Data Modifications
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system enforces electronic signatures for critical actions and maintains a comprehensive audit trail as per 21 CFR Part 11.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User accounts with appropriate permissions are created.
A setpoint for temperature monitoring is established.

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify a temperature setpoint without logging in with an authorized user.
test_steps.expected_result: The system shall prevent the modification and prompt for user authentication.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of error message or prompt

test_steps.action: Log in with an authorized user and modify the temperature setpoint.
test_steps.expected_result: The system shall prompt for an electronic signature (username and password) to confirm the modification.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail for the setpoint modification.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail shall record the date, time, user, action performed (setpoint modification), old value, new value, and the electronic signature confirmation.
data_to_capture: Audit trail log entries for the modification
Details of the recorded audit trail information

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully enforces electronic signatures for setpoint modifications.
The audit trail accurately and completely records all details of the modification, including the electronic signature.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail shall be secure, unalterable, and time-stamped.
Electronic signatures shall be unique and tied to an individual.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Integration with Facility Management and Paging Systems
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS can successfully interface with the existing facility management system and integrate alarm notifications with the site paging system.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
Facility Management System (FMS) is accessible and configured for integration.
Site paging system is accessible and configured for integration.
Network connectivity between systems is established.

test_steps.action: Induce a temperature alarm condition that should trigger an alert to the FMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS shall send an alert notification to the FMS via the defined standard protocol.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the alarm condition in EMS
Confirmation of alert received in FMS logs or interface

test_steps.action: Induce a critical temperature alarm condition that should trigger a notification to the site paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS shall send an alarm notification to the site paging system using the vendor API.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the critical alarm condition in EMS
Confirmation of notification received on the paging system

test_steps.action: Verify that the data exchanged between EMS and FMS is accurate and complete.
test_steps.expected_result: The data (e.g., temperature readings, alarm status) transmitted to the FMS matches the data within the EMS.
data_to_capture: Sample data comparison between EMS and FMS

acceptance_criteria: The EMS successfully transmits alarm notifications to the FMS.
The EMS successfully integrates with the site paging system for critical alarms.
Data integrity is maintained during the integration process.
data_integrity_requirements: Data transmitted to FMS must be accurate and complete.
Alarm notifications must be timely and correctly routed.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Standard Reports for Batch Release
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system utilizes vendor-supplied standard reports for batch release purposes as per URS-EMS-007.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Temperature monitoring is active and data is being recorded.
Access to vendor-supplied standard reports is available.

test_steps.action: Access the reporting module of the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The reporting module is accessible and displays available standard reports.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the reporting module interface.

test_steps.action: Generate a standard temperature report for a defined period (e.g., last 24 hours).
test_steps.expected_result: A report is generated in the vendor's standard format, containing temperature data for the specified period.

test_steps.action: Review the generated report to confirm it contains all relevant temperature data and is in the expected vendor format.
test_steps.expected_result: The report accurately reflects the recorded temperature data and adheres to the vendor's standard report template.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of data accuracy and format adherence.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully generates standard reports as provided by the vendor.
The generated reports are in the vendor's standard format and contain accurate temperature data.
The reports are suitable for use in batch release decisions.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-007: Standard reports provided by vendor shall be used for batch release.
data_integrity_requirements: Report generation must not alter original data.
Report format must be consistent and verifiable.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Data Storage Capacity
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS meets the specified system availability (99.5%) and data storage capacity (minimum 10 years) requirements.
prerequisites: EMS has been operational for a significant period to allow for availability assessment.
System logs and monitoring tools are accessible.
Information on planned maintenance schedules is available.

test_steps.action: Obtain system uptime records for the past 12 months (or longest available period).
test_steps.expected_result: System uptime records are available and can be analyzed.

test_steps.action: Calculate the system availability percentage, excluding planned maintenance periods.
test_steps.expected_result: Calculated availability percentage is equal to or greater than 99.5%.

test_steps.action: Review system configuration and database size to estimate current data storage usage.
test_steps.expected_result: Current data storage usage is documented.

test_steps.action: Based on current data generation rate and storage capacity, project the system's ability to store data for a minimum of 10 years.
test_steps.expected_result: Projection confirms the system can store data for at least 10 years.

acceptance_criteria: System availability is confirmed to be 99.5% or higher, excluding planned maintenance.
The system's data storage capacity is confirmed to support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-012: Data storage capacity shall support minimum 10 years of continuous monitoring.
URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: Uptime calculations must accurately reflect system availability.
Storage capacity projections must be based on realistic data generation rates.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Setpoint Deviation Alerting and Notification Integration
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS generates alerts when temperature deviates from setpoints and that these notifications integrate with the site paging system.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational.
Site paging system is accessible and configured for integration.
User has administrative access to the EMS and paging system.

test_steps.action: Configure a specific GMP storage area's temperature setpoint within the EMS (e.g., 20°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The setpoint is successfully configured and saved in the EMS.

test_steps.action: Manually adjust the temperature in the configured storage area to exceed the setpoint by more than 2°C (e.g., 22.1°C or higher).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS detects the temperature deviation and generates an alert.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alert notification is sent to the site paging system via the vendor API.
test_steps.expected_result: An alert notification is received on the designated paging system, containing relevant details of the temperature deviation.

test_steps.action: Return the temperature to within the acceptable range.
test_steps.expected_result: The alert status in the EMS is cleared, and any subsequent 'clear' notification is sent to the paging system if configured.
data_to_capture: Clear notification on paging system (if applicable)

acceptance_criteria: The EMS successfully generates an alert when the temperature deviates by more than 2°C from the configured setpoint.
The alert notification is accurately transmitted to the site paging system.
The alert notification contains all necessary information (e.g., area, temperature, deviation).
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-005: The system shall generate alerts when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint.
URS-EMS-015: Alarm notifications shall integrate with site paging system using vendor API.
data_integrity_requirements: Alert generation and notification logs must be accurate and complete.
Audit trail must record alert generation and clearing events.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Standard Reports for Batch Release and Data Archival
test_cases.objective: To verify that the vendor's standard reports are usable for batch release and that the system's archival feature correctly retains data for the specified period.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists to test reporting and archival.
User has access to generate vendor standard reports.
User has access to the system's archival mechanism.

test_steps.action: Generate a standard temperature and humidity report for a specific period (e.g., one month) using the vendor's built-in reporting functionality.
test_steps.expected_result: The report is generated successfully and contains accurate, complete, and legible data for the selected period.

test_steps.action: Review the generated report to confirm it meets the requirements for batch release (e.g., includes all critical data points, is easily interpretable).
test_steps.expected_result: The report is deemed suitable for batch release purposes, containing all necessary information in a clear format.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of report suitability for batch release
Any observations or deviations from expected report content

test_steps.action: Initiate the vendor's archival process for historical data, ensuring it covers a period exceeding 7 years.
test_steps.expected_result: The archival process completes successfully, and data older than 7 years is moved to the archive.
data_to_capture: Archival process start and end timestamps
Details of data archived (e.g., date range)

test_steps.action: Verify that data older than 7 years is no longer readily accessible in the primary database but can be retrieved from the archive.
test_steps.expected_result: Primary database shows no data older than 7 years, and a sample of archived data can be successfully retrieved and verified for integrity.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of primary database data range

acceptance_criteria: Vendor standard reports are generated accurately and are suitable for batch release.
The system's archival feature successfully retains data for a minimum of 7 years.
Archived data is retrievable and maintains its integrity.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-007: Standard reports provided by vendor shall be used for batch release.
URS-EMS-010: Data shall be retained for 7 years using vendor's archival feature.
data_integrity_requirements: Reports must accurately reflect the data stored.
Archived data must be protected from unauthorized modification or deletion.
Audit trail must record archival and retrieval events.
